Does this sound familiar?

Your CRM has plenty of contacts—but you're not completely sure which records are accurate, who needs follow-up, or which opportunities may already be slipping through the cracks.

Outdated or unreliable data

Duplicate contacts, missing information, old job titles, and inconsistent fields make it difficult to know which records you can actually trust.

Leads getting lost in the pipeline

Some contacts have been followed up. Others haven't. And when statuses and next steps aren't clear, it's easy for promising leads to sit untouched.

Too much manual checking

Your team relies on spreadsheets, notes, memory, or repeated manual checks just to figure out what happened and what needs to happen next.

Your CRM should make follow-up easier—not create more work.

CRM support that starts with the foundation

Whether your CRM needs a cleanup, better organization, or a more reliable follow-up process, I start by understanding what's already there and what's getting in the way.

Where most clients start

1. CRM audit & data cleanup

I review your CRM to identify outdated, duplicated, incomplete, or inconsistent records, then clean and standardize the data so it's easier to manage and trust.

This can include: database audits, duplicate review, contact verification, missing-field updates, data standardization, and identifying outdated records.

2. Contact & lead qualification

Not every contact in your CRM deserves the same attention. I research and verify contacts and companies, then organize them based on the criteria that matter to your business.

This can include: LinkedIn and company research, decision-maker verification, lead qualification, and categorizing contacts for follow-up or further review.

3. CRM structure & pipeline setup

I help organize your CRM so it's clear where contacts and opportunities stand—and what needs to happen next.

This can include: pipeline stages, contact statuses, custom fields, naming conventions, and clearer processes for moving leads through your CRM.

4. Follow-up & CRM automation

Once the data and process are clear, I can help set up practical automations that reduce repetitive follow-up and keep your CRM organized.

This can include: inquiry follow-ups, reminders, lead nurturing, status-based workflows, and simple automations that stop or change when a contact books, responds, unsubscribes, or converts.

Real CRM problems, practical fixes

Two recent projects, and how I approached them.

HubSpotCRM platform

CRM database cleanup and contact verification

The problem
A large CRM database contained incomplete location data, outdated employment information, and inconsistent contact records—making segmentation, compliance checks, and future outreach less reliable.
What I did
I reviewed contact records individually, using LinkedIn and available company information to verify employment and location details. I updated and standardized Country/Region data and identified contacts who had left their companies or required further review.
The result
A cleaner and more reliable CRM database with standardized location data and better visibility into outdated records—giving the team stronger data for segmentation, compliance, and future outreach.

Lead qualification and prospect research

The problem
The client uses Apollo to source potential leads, but the search results still required manual review before outreach. Job titles and company information alone weren't always enough to determine whether each contact and company matched the client's ideal customer profile.
What I did
I reviewed and qualified prospects sourced through Apollo, then used LinkedIn and available company information to verify company relevance and decision-maker roles against the client's qualification criteria. Each record was categorized as Qualified, Needs Review, or Not a Fit.
The result
A more focused prospect database with clearer qualification decisions, helping the client prioritize relevant contacts and spend less time reviewing unsuitable leads.

How each record was sorted

Every contact was checked against the client's ideal customer profile.

QualifiedMatches the profile and is ready for outreach
Needs reviewPotential fit, needs more research
Not a fitOutside the target profile, so no outreach

Your CRM data is treated with care

CRM cleanup often means working with important customer and prospect information. I keep the process careful and controlled.

  • Access you control. I work through the access you provide and can start with limited permissions where appropriate.
  • Backup before bulk changes. I recommend an export or backup before major updates are made.
  • No deletions without approval. Records that may need removing are flagged for review first.

Questions people ask

How long does a CRM cleanup take?

It depends on the size of your database and the condition of the data. Once I understand what needs attention, I'll give you a clear scope and timeline before the cleanup begins.

Which CRMs do you work with?

Most of my recent CRM work has been in HubSpot. If you use another platform, tell me what you're working with and I'll let you know whether it's a good fit for my services.

What do you need from me to get started?

Usually, I'll need an overview of the problem you're trying to solve, access to your CRM or a relevant export, and someone I can ask questions when business rules or contact history need clarification.
